heroHeadline: GSF Under New Commander Batsuuri; BINUH: 78+ Killed in Cité Soleil Clashes Since May 9 — MSF Hospital Closed Day 7, Artibonite Crisis Ongoing
heroSubtitle: Major General Erdenebat Batsuuri of Mongolia formally assumed command of the UN-authorized Gang Suppression Force (GSF) on May 14, 2026, becoming the first non-Kenyan commander of an international security mission in Haiti — with approximately 800 personnel now deployed from Chad, Guatemala, and El Salvador but still concentrated exclusively in Port-au-Prince's city center. On the same day, UN BINUH released a provisional toll of at least 78 killed and 66 wounded since May 9 from intra-Viv Ansanm gang clashes in Cité Soleil and Croix-des-Bouquets, with at least 10 confirmed civilian deaths; between March 5 and May 11, the same two communes saw 305 killed and 277 wounded — including 63 confirmed civilian residents (17 women, 13 children). MSF's Cité Soleil hospital — the only emergency medical facility for the commune's 300,000+ residents — remained closed for a seventh consecutive day as of May 16, with no public reopening timeline. OCHA published Artibonite Flash Update No. 2 on May 15, confirming the security crisis extends far beyond Port-au-Prince: Gran Grif and Kokorat San Ras continue consolidating control along Route Nationale 1, with no GSF presence in the department. In a modest positive development, the Dominican Republic reopened its airspace to Cap-Haïtien in May 2026 after approximately two years of suspension. PM Fils-Aimé's May 12 declaration that August 30 elections are 'impossible' remains in force; no electoral decree has been issued; 23 communes are inaccessible; 1.47M+ Haitians remain internally displaced; 5.9M face acute food insecurity; the 2026 HRP is funded at only ~20% of its $880M target. The Washington Post investigation (May 15) documented ~$970M in US Haiti security spending since 2024 against expanding gang control.
